title: CLI: Streamline Node.js version detection code
body:
## What I did

Improved old node runtime warnings and ensured the min version declaration is well centralised.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing


1. Create a test project
2. Run `npx storybook@latest init` with a non-supported Node runtime (e.g., 22.x)
3. Observe the warning correctly displays min versions
4. Run other SB commands with an out-of-date Node version
5. Observe the same warning
6. Run a SB command with an outrageously out of date Node version
7. Watch the CLI crash; not much can be done about that

### Documentation

ø

## Checklist for Maintainers

- [x] When this PR is ready for testing, make sure to add `ci:normal`, `ci:merged` or `ci:daily` GH label to it to run a specific set of sandboxes. The particular set of sandboxes can be found in `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/sandbox-templates.ts`
- [x] Make sure this PR contains **one** of the labels below:

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Interactive preflight now detects declared Node versions and prompts to update .nvmrc or package.json engines when below Storybook's minimum, with selectable target versions and graceful skip/CI behavior.
  * CLI now uses a centralized human-readable minimum-version message when the runtime is unsupported.

* **Refactor**
  * Centralized Node.js minimum-version policy and validation used across CLI and setup flows.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive tests for parsing, detection, validation, prompts, and update flows.

author: Sidnioulz

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `detectDeclaredNodeVersions()` searches for `.nvmrc` all the way up the directory tree (`find.up('.nvmrc', { cwd })`). When `sb init` is run from a subdirectory (or inside a non-repo folder), this can accidentally pick up and later *modify* an unrelated `.nvmrc` (e.g. one in the user’s home directory). Consider bounding the search with `last: getProjectRoot()` (or otherwise limiting it to the intended project root) so we only ever read/update project-owned files.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
@copilot apply changes based on [this feedback](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/34440#discussion_r3032960978)

Also add a unit test for that if possible.

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body: Done in 89c5d2d. `detectDeclaredNodeVersions()` now passes `last: getProjectRoot()` to `find.up('.nvmrc', ...)`, bounding the upward search to the project root (same pattern used by `findFilesUp` in `paths.ts`). Two unit tests were added: one verifying `find.up` is called with the correct `{ cwd, last }` options, and one verifying that `nvmrcPath` is `undefined` when the mock simulates no `.nvmrc` within the project root.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `parseNodeVersionString()` treats major-only values like `"22"` or `"20"` as `22.0.0` / `20.0.0`. In `.nvmrc`, major-only is a common way to mean “latest 22.x”, which should be considered supported under the stated policy (20.19+ or 22.12+). As-is, `.nvmrc: 22` will be flagged as unsupported and trigger a bump prompt. Consider preserving the input’s precision (major vs major.minor vs full) and adjusting the support check accordingly for major-only declarations.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
@copilot apply changes based on [this feedback](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/34440#discussion_r3032960990)

Add a parameter to check if we use nvmrc logic (treat missing bits as latest, so as long as the present bits are equal or higher, we're good) or semver logic (in which case 22 is treated as 22.0.0 because we want to ensure that we bump the version to e.g. 22.22.1)

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body:
Done in 495ace2. `parseNodeVersionString` now returns a `precision: 'major' | 'minor' | 'patch'` field tracking how many version components were present. `isNodeVersionSupported` gains an optional `{ mode, precision }` parameter:

- `mode: 'nvmrc'` + `precision: 'major'` (e.g. `.nvmrc: 22`): supported if major 22 exists in `MIN_SUPPORTED_NODE_VERSIONS` (i.e. "latest 22.x" is valid)
- `mode: 'nvmrc'` + `precision: 'minor'` (e.g. `.nvmrc: 22.14`): supported if `22.14 >= 22.12` at the minor level
- `mode: 'nvmrc'` + `precision: 'patch'` or `mode: 'strict'` (default): current strict behavior

Both `.nvmrc` check paths in `PreflightCheckCommand` and `node-version-check.ts` now use `{ mode: 'nvmrc', precision: parsed.precision }`.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `updateEnginesNode()` claims to preserve formatting, but it only infers a numeric indent width and always rewrites via `JSON.stringify`, which will reformat minified JSON and can’t preserve tabs/newlines/key ordering/comments. Also, `indentMatch[1].length` will turn tab-indented JSON into spaces. Consider using the same indentation detection approach as `JsPackageManager` (it uses `detect-indent`) and/or soften the docstring to match actual behavior.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: @copilot apply changes based on [this feedback](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/34440#discussion_r3032961000)

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body: Done in 495ace2. `updateEnginesNode` now uses `detect-indent` (already used by `JsPackageManager`) to detect indentation. The detected `indent` string (e.g. `"\t"` for tabs, `"  "` for 2-space) is passed directly to `JSON.stringify`, preserving tab-indented files correctly. Falls back to 2-space indent when no indentation is detected (e.g. minified JSON).

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: This new flow can prompt the user during `execute()`, but it doesn’t respect `--yes` / non-interactive/CI runs. `prompt.select` will still attempt an interactive clack prompt even when `process.stdin/stdout` aren’t TTYs (the prompt layer doesn’t auto-disable for selects), which can hang automated usage. Consider skipping the prompt (and just logging the warning) when `options.yes === true` and/or when the terminal isn’t interactive / `process.env.CI` is set.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: @copilot apply changes based on [this feedback](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/34440#discussion_r3032961017)

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body: Done in 495ace2. `options.yes` is now threaded through `execute` → `checkDeclaredNodeVersion(yes)` → `promptVersionBump(..., yes)`. The interactive guard is now `!yes && process.stdout.isTTY && process.stdin.isTTY && !process.env.CI && !process.env.STORYBOOK_CI`, so passing `--yes` skips the bump prompt (same as CI/non-TTY environments).

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
Sidnioulz
comments.body: @copilot take that into account

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body: Already addressed in the previous commit (89c5d2d) — `updateNvmrc`/`updateEnginesNode` calls in `promptVersionBump` are wrapped in try/catch with a `logger.warn` that lets init continue on failure.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: For the `engines.node` “current runtime” option, the value is set to `>=${runtimeVersion}` (includes patch), while the minimum options are `>=${major}.${minor}` (no patch). This makes the runtime option unnecessarily strict (e.g. `>=22.14.2`) and inconsistent with the other choices. Consider using `>=${runtimeMajor}.${runtimeMinor}` (or otherwise aligning the formatting with the minimum-version options).

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `handleUnsupportedNodeRuntime()` can also prompt via `prompt.select`, but there’s no guard for non-interactive/CI usage. On an unsupported Node runtime in CI, this can hang instead of exiting with an error. Consider detecting non-interactive environments (e.g. `!process.stdin.isTTY || !process.stdout.isTTY || process.env.CI`) and skipping the bump prompt in that case (just print the error and exit).

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: @copilot apply changes based on [this feedback](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/34440#discussion_r3032961059)

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: If both `.nvmrc` and `package.json#engines.node` are bumped in the same run, the exit message only mentions `.nvmrc` (because it branches on `nvmrcBumped` first) and silently omits that `engines.node` was also updated. Consider emitting a combined message when both were changed so the user gets accurate instructions/context.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Only one is checked and updated AFAIK. Verify this before making any code change. If only one is checked (i.e. if the first check for nvmrc returns a need to bump, and also enforces that there wont be a check on the package engine), then do not change this piece of logic.

🌐 Web query:

`semver minVersion OR-range union behavior "||"`

💡 Result:

In npm's semver implementation (node-semver), the "||" operator in version ranges creates a union of comparator sets. A version satisfies the range if it satisfies at least one of the sets separated by "||". Within each set (separated by spaces), comparators form an intersection—all must be satisfied. For example: - ">=1.2.7 <1.3.0" matches versions >=1.2.7 AND <1.3.0. - "1.2.7 || >=1.2.9 <2.0.0" matches 1.2.7 OR (versions >=1.2.9 AND <2.0.0). The minVersion(range) function returns the lowest possible version that satisfies the range, which for an OR-range ("A || B || C") is the minimum of minVersion(A), minVersion(B), and minVersion(C). Example: minVersion('14.0.0 || 16.1.0 || 18.0.0') returns '14.0.0'. This behavior is standard in npm, Yarn, and compatible tools. The core semver.org spec defines version formats but not ranges; node-semver provides the de facto range specification used by the JS ecosystem. Pre-releases are not included by default unless explicitly specified in a comparator or with {includePrerelease: true}.

Citations:

- 1: https://semver-nuget.org/v2.3.x/Semver.html
- 2: https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/dependency-versions
- 3: https://github.com/npm/node-semver/issues/649
- 4: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v6/using-npm/semver/
- 5: https://github.com/npm/node-semver/
- 6: https://registry.npmjs.org/semver
- 7: https://github.com/npm/npm/blob/d081cc6/doc/misc/semver.md
- 8: https://npm.github.io/using-pkgs-docs/package-json/types-of-dependencies.html

**`minVersion()` incorrectly flags version ranges that include supported Node.js versions.**

For a value like `>=18 <19 || >=20.19.0`, `minVersion()` returns `18.0.0`, causing this code to warn and offer to rewrite a range that already includes supported Storybook versions (20.19.0, 22.12.0+, etc.). The check collapses the entire OR-union to its absolute minimum rather than testing whether any part of the union satisfies `isNodeVersionSupported()`. Evaluate the comparator sets individually or centralize this logic in the shared node-version util.

The same issue exists in `code/lib/create-storybook/src/node-version-check.ts:52-68`.

Also applies to lines 178-181.

<details>

```

In `@code/lib/create-storybook/src/commands/PreflightCheckCommand.ts` around lines
154 - 157, The logic using minVersion(declared.enginesNode) incorrectly
collapses OR-ranges; instead determine whether any alternative in the range
already allows a supported Node by splitting the range into its comparator sets
and testing each set against isNodeVersionSupported, or better yet add a shared
helper (e.g., isRangeSupported(range) in the node-version util) that returns
true if any comparator-set satisfies isNodeVersionSupported. Replace the current
minVersion+isNodeVersionSupported checks in PreflightCheckCommand (where
declared.enginesNode is used to potentially call promptVersionBump) and the
analogous block in node-version-check.ts with calls to this new helper (or
implement the split-and-test logic inline) so you only prompt to rewrite ranges
that contain no supported comparator-set.
```

</details>
